clue.text: Said "when" with Old- Fashioned ?

definitions.meaning: to say when something happened is to give it a date, past tense
out of date, belonging to a past style

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: assigned a time of origin, and gone out of style with the years.

clue.text: To offend is to ask for a ticket to Hell

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for Hell itself
at a booking office you name the destination and add please

explanation.surface: Someone saying that buying a ticket to the underworld is an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Asking for a ticket to Hell, you would say 'Dis, please'; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To displease someone is to annoy or upset them.

clue.text: Object that's a bit of an obsession

definitions.meaning: to have a ... about something is to be fixated on it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an article or item, and in the idiom 'have a thing about' a mild fixation.

clue.text: The tender beauty of tact

definitions.meaning: fineness and fragility, a dainty grace

explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers fineness and fragility of form, and also sensitivity in dealing with awkward matters.

clue.text: It's for every old actor

parts.note: per is the Latin word meaning for each, as in a price per head
former means old in the sense of earlier, from times gone by

explanation.surface: A remark that something belongs to every veteran actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link: PER (for every) plus FORMER (old) builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is one who plays roles on stage, a kind of entertainer giving a show.

clue.text: A mere game

definitions.meaning: a mere is a lake or pond
a cue game played on a table with pockets

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a small body of still water, and also a billiards-type game.

clue.text: As a cure it's in fact about the same — though going up

indicators.note: the in-fact word goes round, or about, the reversed Latin word

parts.note: really means actually, in fact

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: idem is Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A remark that a treatment is really much the same but improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses the Latin word in this down clue; 'it's' and 'though' are links. The surface reads 'about the same' as roughly equal, but 'about' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial means serving to cure or put right, so the adverb means by way of a remedy.

clue.text: Short piece of music — one not involved for choice

parts.note: op. is the short form of opus, a musical work

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A brief musical number, with one player not taking part, as a matter of choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges I plus NOT to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is an alternative you are free to take, a selection.

clue.text: Poor Rita, in progress of time a dominant old lady

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes inside the word for the progress of time

parts.note: the march of time is its steady progress

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor Rita, grown old over the years, rules the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges the name to TRIA. The 'march of time' is the idiom behind 'progress of time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is the female head of a family, often its elderly ruler.

clue.text: Man ran in Xanadu

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for run or runs, as in cricket scores
Alph is the sacred river that ran through Xanadu in Coleridge's Kubla Khan

explanation.surface: A man running in Kubla Khan's fabled city.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's poem has 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran', so 'ran in Xanadu' also points to the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a man's given name.

clue.text: Where the drink is not yet -full

definitions.meaning: a household room once used for distilling cordials and storing liquor and preserves
read as a phrase: there is space left, so more can go in

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen before 'full' is a printing mark from a line break; the clue reads 'not yet full'.
explanation.definitionFit: The household distilling room took its name from the still; and 'still room' means space remains, so the vessel is unfilled.

clue.text: Complete result of casting

definitions.meaning: utter, absolute, as in a complete disaster
casting up a column of figures means adding it, and the sum it gives

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for utter or entire and a noun for the sum reached when figures are cast up, an old term for adding.

clue.text: Second best bed, for instance, in crochet-like borders

indicators.note: the abbreviation for for instance goes inside the lacy word, which borders it on each side

parts.note: crochet work is openwork like lace, so crochet-like means lacy
e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: Describing a bed with crocheted edging as an example of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' says the same as 'in': LACY borders, or surrounds, EG. Shakespeare's will famously left his wife his 'second best bed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bequeathed in a will is an inheritance, and Shakespeare's will left his widow his second best bed.

clue.text: Warn a pretty girl about Scotsman

indicators.note: the pretty girl word goes round, or about, the Scots word for a man

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: Advice to caution an attractive young woman about a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty girl' hides old slang: a 'dish' is an attractive person. Mon is how a Scot says man.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to caution or reprove, giving someone a warning.

clue.text: If you know of a wetter hole, go to it

definitions.text: If you know of a wetter hole, go to it

parts.words: If you know of a wetter hole, go to it
parts.note: a golfer's name for the clubhouse bar, the drinking stop after the eighteen holes of the course

explanation.definitionFit: Golfers call the clubhouse bar the hole after the last, where the drinking happens.

clue.text: Bloody politely — for a grammarian!

parts.note: the swear word bloody is used as a describing word, so a polite speaker names it by its grammatical class instead of saying it

explanation.definitionFit: Polite speakers once replaced 'bloody' by naming its part of speech, a euphemism used as a qualifier word.

clue.text: David's: dad embraces a small minute flower-girl

indicators.note: the dad's name holds the other pieces inside it, as in an embrace

parts.note: in the Bible Jesse is the father of King David
min is the abbreviation, a shortened form, of minute

explanation.surface: King David's father hugging a tiny flower girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is a printing mark: the page reads 'David's dad'. 'small' marks the abbreviation of minute; the pieces sit inside the biblical name before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessamine is an old name for jasmine, a fragrant climbing plant, and also a girl's given name.

clue.text: Fall for a drink

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a decline or plunge, and also a small measure of spirits offered to a guest.

clue.text: What Tosti wrote for some singers?

definitions.text: What Tosti wrote for some singers?

parts.words: What Tosti wrote for some singers?
parts.note: the composer Tosti wrote songs, and some singers sing in parts, as in choral pieces for several voices

explanation.walkthrough: Francesco Paolo Tosti was an Italian composer of popular Victorian drawing-room songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral pieces arranged for several voices in harmony go by this name.

clue.text: A carving-knife victim was big-headed and over-matey

indicators.note: headed means this piece comes at the head, before the rest

parts.note: taken from big-headed

indicators.note: the farmer's wife cut off the tails of the three blind mice with a carving knife, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a mouse was the victim in the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice

explanation.surface: A conceited victim of a knife attack who was too friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off the mice's tails with a carving knife, so MOUSE loses its tail E. BIG goes at the head, hence 'big-headed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamist has two spouses, too many partners or mates at once.

clue.text: Singest of summer in full-… throated (Keats)

definitions.text: Singest of summer in full-… throated (Keats)

parts.words: Singest of summer in full-… throated (Keats)
parts.note: the missing word completes a line of Keats's Ode to a Nightingale, where the bird sings of summer with full-throated relaxation

explanation.walkthrough: The gap is the word missing from the quotation, which reads 'Singest of summer in full-throated ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's nightingale sings without strain, in full-throated comfort and freedom.

clue.text: Where Will's so different he's for you

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are made different, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the name Will with its s, all five letters used

explanation.surface: Asking where a man named Will is so unlike himself, and then saying he is on your side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so different' signals the anagram of WHERE plus WILLS, all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is for you supports you and hopes good things come your way.

clue.text: Retiring and small

explanation.definitionFit: The word means unassuming and shy, and also of limited size or amount.

clue.text: Fish was in debt-has to be. — followed

parts.note: the shad is a herring-like fish
owed means had a debt to pay

explanation.surface: A fishy borrower who must be pursued for what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to be' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them, so the past tense means trailed.

clue.text: A beating on the feet

definitions.meaning: to give someone ... is old slang for thrashing them
garments worn on the feet inside shoes

explanation.definitionFit: The plural is old slang for a thrashing, and names the knitted garments worn under shoes.

clue.text: Scornful address set back this boatman

indicators.note: set back means the word is turned round and read from the end

parts.note: sirrah is an old contemptuous form of address to a man or boy

explanation.surface: A boatman being addressed with contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' reverses SIRRAH. Harris is one of the boating friends in Jerome K. Jerome's novel Three Men in a Boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris rows up the Thames in Three Men in a Boat, a comic Victorian novel about a river trip.

clue.text: Lift shafts, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for shafts is heard spoken and gives a word of the same sound

parts.note: rays are shafts of light

explanation.surface: Lift shafts that only seem so, judging by noise.
explanation.walkthrough: RAYS, shafts of light, sounds like the verb for lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to elevate it.

clue.text: For a change hands up !

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: paws is slang for hands

explanation.surface: A command to raise your hands, for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PAWS in this down clue. 'For' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange of one thing for another is a swap.

clue.text: Proverbially 'a.welsher? It's something wicked!

parts.note: a welsher is one who fails to pay a debt, and the proverb says wrongdoing never pays either

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Proverbially a welsher?' with no stray marks. The proverb is 'crime doesn't pay', so it behaves like a welsher, who doesn't pay up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawbreaking is wicked conduct, and the proverb says it does not pay off.

clue.text: Scots lad follows, latest fashion of a scientist

indicators.note: the Scots lad comes after, following the other pieces

parts.note: the latest thing is new
ton is an old word for fashion or high style
Ian is a common Scottish boy's name

explanation.surface: A young Scotsman keeping up with the newest style.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to Isaac Newton, the physicist of gravity and motion.

clue.text: Whose, step wanders to a children's Mecca'?

indicators.note: the letters of the words wander about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whose footsteps stray towards a place children love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanders' rearranges WHOSE plus STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling confectionery draws children as Mecca draws pilgrims.

clue.text: Necessary measures for wall paper-hangers.

parts.note: measures read as actions taken, but decorators need a folding ladder to reach the top of a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A folding stepladder is the kit decorators climb to hang paper high on a wall.
